parts.name: nbn HFC NTD (Arris CM8200B)
parts.notes: The nbn connection box for HFC (DOCSIS 3.1), black. Stands upright (can be turned on its side in the planner): 132 mm tall × 44 mm wide × 132 mm deep, 0.95 kg (5.19 × 1.73 × 5.19 in, 2.1 lb per a reseller copy of the Arris datasheet). 2 × gigabit Ethernet (UNI-D1/UNI-D2; nbn normally activates UNI-D1 only), one F-type coax input, 12 V DC in. Power draw not published.

powerInput.notes: 12 V DC plug-pack supplied by nbn. The 2 A rating comes from DeviWiki, not an Arris datasheet.

layout.notes: Front follows product photos: nbn mark, POWER / DOWNSTREAM / UPSTREAM / ONLINE LEDs, ARRIS and CM8200 at the bottom (plain text, no logos). Datasheet: Ethernet link/speed LEDs on the rear. Rear connector order (coax at the top, then UNI-D1, UNI-D2, reset, DC jack) and all offsets are estimated.

parts.name: nbn FTTP NTD, 1 port (Nokia XS-010X-Q)
parts.notes: The 1-port nbn fibre connection box (XGS-PON), white. 135 × 135 × 30 mm, 12 V DC 1 A, under 8.6 W, per Nokia's XS-010X-Q datasheet; one SC/APC fibre input (simplex) and one 100M–10G RJ45 (nbn runs it at up to 2.5 Gbps). Weight left blank: Nokia's datasheet says 0.366 kg, its quick reference guide 0.285 kg. nbn's unit is wall-mounted under a cover and relabels the lights Power / Optical / Alarm / Port.

powerInput.notes: 12 V DC plug-pack supplied by nbn.

layout.notes: Port edge follows Nokia's product photo (PON, ETHERNET, RESET, POWER, ON/OFF), drawn as the rear; nbn says the order can vary. Light names from nbn's 1-port page. Offsets estimated. Top view: lights at the corner away from the ports, NOKIA near the port edge, as in Nokia's photo. The front edge label is the planner's own, to tell the boxes apart.

parts.name: nbn FTTC connection device (NetComm NDD-0300)
parts.notes: The nbn FTTC connection box (VDSL2/G.fast over the phone line), white, lies flat. 166 × 118 × 44 mm from retailer listings (no NetComm datasheet found). Mains cord straight in (cloverleaf C6 inlet); it also powers the nbn kerbside unit over the phone line, so its draw is not a normal modem's and is not published. GATEWAY is the Ethernet port to your router; WALL SOCKET is the RJ11 phone line in from the wall.

powerInput.notes: nbn mains cord (C5 plug) into the POWER inlet.

layout.notes: Port order and names from nbn's FTTC setup guide photos (POWER, WALL SOCKET, RESET, GATEWAY); lights LAN / DSL / Connection / Power under a slide cover on the top. Offsets estimated. GATEWAY jack is yellow as on the unit. The front edge label is the planner's own, to tell the boxes apart.

parts.name: nbn Fixed Wireless connection box
parts.notes: The indoor box for nbn Fixed Wireless, white, normally wall-mounted; modelled lying on its back with the port edge to the rear. Face about 220 × 127 mm (Internode's guide, original model; nbn says the current box is similar in size). Thickness, weight, power draw and port speed not published, so it takes 2U and the height is left blank. 4 × UNI-D data ports; the antenna cable and power lead sit under a tamper-proof cover and aren't cable ends in the planner.

powerInput.notes: Plug-pack supplied by nbn; the box end is a fixed lead under the tamper-proof cover, not a barrel jack. Voltage not published.

layout.notes: Port edge from nbn's 2024 user guide drawing: covered power and antenna lead on the left, 4 × UNI-D on the right. Lights (Power, Status, Outdoor unit, 3-step signal strength) sit under a cover on the face. Offsets estimated. The front edge label is the planner's own, to tell the boxes apart.

parts.name: Raspberry Pi 4 in official case (red/white)
parts.notes: Placed with the USB/Ethernet end facing the front, so the footprint is 70 mm wide × 97 mm deep. Case size 97 × 70 × 25 mm per RS Components (Raspberry Pi doesn't publish case dimensions). Power: 600 mA typical bare-board draw (3 W), 3.0 A supply recommended, up to 1.2 A for USB peripherals. USB-C power, two micro HDMI and audio are on the long left side, microSD and the power/activity LEDs at the far end.

powerInput.notes: Needs a 5.1 V / 3 A USB-C supply (official 15.3 W PSU recommended); not included with the board.

layout.notes: Port order on the end face (USB 2.0 pair, USB 3.0 pair, Ethernet) follows the Pi 4 board; exact offsets in the case are estimated. The top view shows the side connectors (USB-C power, micro HDMI 0/1, audio) on the left long side, spaced as on the Pi 4 board.
